## Who I Am

I'm a PhD researcher in Psychology at the [University of Hull](https://www.hull.ac.uk/), funded by the [White Rose Doctoral Training Partnership (WRDTP)](https://wrdtp.ac.uk/). My work sits at the intersection of human cognition and artificial intelligence — I'm interested in how our minds adapt, resist, and evolve as AI becomes harder to tell apart from reality.

My MSc research (Distinction) explored how people judge the authenticity of AI-altered images: how we cognitively process AI-generated images differently from real photographs, and what happens when the line between the two blurs. My PhD is now extending that into joint-action settings, examining whether the social Inhibition of Return effect persists when the other actor in a task is an AI rather than a person. I'm also broadly interested in the wider social and philosophical fallout of an AI-saturated world — from AI-generated misinformation to what "real" and "fake" even mean anymore. (More of this shows up on my [blog](blog.qmd)!)

Before Hull, I completed my BSc in Psychology at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore, where I was twice named an NTU President Research Scholar through the Undergraduate Research Experience on Campus (URECA) programme, leading two independent, year-long research projects along the way. Full academic history is on my [CV](CV.qmd).
